newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks end higher on economic optimism.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks end higher on economic optimism.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange closed higher on Friday thanks to optimism on Peru's macroeconomic progress and a return of foreign investors, brokers said.
They predicted further gains on Monday, given these local factors and the knock-on effect of regional gains.

"Today there was plenty of buying in the market. The volume shows the entry of foreign investors who are expecting a rise based on the macroeconomic performance in the first half," said Enrique Hernandez, of Macrovalores brokerage.
The General Index .IGRA gained 1.59 percent to 1,572.81 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index was up 1.18 percent to 2,091.77.
Total market volume was a healthy 41 million soles ($16.4 million) on 2,217 trades. Overall, 62 stocks rose, 21 fell and 33 were unchanged.

Food company Consorcio de Alimentos Fabril Pacfico accounted for 20 percent of market trade, rising 1.35 percent to 3.75 soles on 8.3 million shares, while benchmark Telefnica del Per lost 0.71 percent to 5.59 soles on 6.0 million shares.

Breweries performed strongly, with Compaa Nacional de Cerveza (CNC) rising 10.19 percent to 1.19 soles on 3.7 million shares, and Backus y Johnston gaining 2.96 percent to 2.78 soles on 3.4 million shares.
These stocks were helped by rumors that the Backus group, which also controls CNC, is considering creating a new holding company, brokers said.
